The *Paṭhamasuṇisāvimānavatthu* ("Daughter-in-Law Mansion", Vv 13) is a canonical poem in the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts how the simple act of offering a single oil cake to the noble Sangha produces substantial karmic merit, resulting in celestial rebirth in a divine mansion (*vimāna*) [SuttaCentral]. The SuttaCentral database records translations of the text across five modern languages [SuttaCentral].

While SuttaCentral does not record any curated cross-canonical parallels for this discourse [SuttaCentral], automated analysis through DharmaNexus highlights significant internal text reuse across the Pali corpus, identifying 198 matching passages shared with 33 texts [DharmaNexus]. The text is extensively cited and explained in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (matching segments §1.1–9.1), with further overlaps occurring in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Significant structural and formulaic parallels occur within the *Vimānavatthu* itself, most notably with the companion text *Dutiyasuṇisāvimānavatthu* (Vv 14, sharing §0.1–9.1), *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), and *Tiladakkhiṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 10) [DharmaNexus]. Across linguistic traditions, DharmaNexus notes weak formulaic alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Jātakamālā* (D4150), though these reflect stock poetic phrasing rather than historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
